promptAsSent:
Use the image_gen tool to generate exactly one image, then stop. Do not write files, run commands or edit anything.

Attached reference images, in order:
Image 1: Layout authority: the six squares and their colours
Image 2: Material/finish only; not layout

Use case: texture map generation / material swatch sheet for a 3D model.
INPUT 1 is a layout sheet of SIX flat-coloured squares in two rows of three on a plain flat mid-blue background. Each square is one hull material of one 3D spacecraft (a Falcon-class light cruiser in a pirate band's hand-applied repaint, a hard-used pirate flagship), to be painted as a flat, square-on texture sample of that material:
top-left square: muted dark khaki-brown armour paint;
top-middle square: dull brick pirate-red paint;
top-right square: light sand-tan paint;
bottom-left square: warm mid grey painted plate;
bottom-middle square: dark gunmetal grey steel machinery;
bottom-right square: the recess material, near-black dull steel.
INPUT 2 is the SAME ship, already painted: it is the finish to match. Use its paint colours, sheen, seams, fasteners and its wear. Never copy INPUT 2's composition, view or shapes.

Paint each square as a texture swatch of its material. Each square will be cut out and tiled many times across the model's small fittings, so:
- Keep the six squares exactly where they are, the same size, with the same plain blue gutters between them. Do not zoom, crop, shift, rotate, enlarge or shrink anything. Each square is filled edge to edge with its material, right up to its straight edges, with nothing drawn outside it.
- Each square is a flat, seen-square-on sample of heavy, hard-used warship plate: a fine, even, all-over surface. Only sparse, small detail: a few thin, faint plate seams and a few small scattered fasteners, even scuffing, an even film of grime. The detail is small and evenly distributed over the whole square, with no single dominant feature: no large rivet rows, no seam or panel line across the middle, no hatches, panels, grilles, labels, stripes or markings, nothing centred.
- Keep each square's colour exactly: khaki stays dark khaki-brown, red stays brick red, sand stays sand tan, grey stays mid grey, gunmetal stays dark grey steel, near-black stays near-black. No colour changes, no repair patches, no different-coloured plates.
- Wear is moderate and even across each whole square. No rust, soot, scorch marks, burns, impact damage, dents, holes, large stains or any concentrated area of wear.
- Lighting: flat, even, shadowless, like an albedo/diffuse texture map. No cast shadows, no ambient-occlusion darkening, no specular highlights, no reflections, no vignette, no directional light, no gradient across a square, no bright border or chipped edge line round a square.
- Background and gutters: the same plain flat uniform mid-blue as INPUT 1, with no floor, shadow, text, labels or borders.
Output: one landscape 16:9 image, same composition as INPUT 1.

references.role: Layout authority: the six squares and their colours

agentMessages: I’ll generate one swatch sheet using Image 1’s exact layout and colours, with Image 2 guiding only the surface finish.
